card.title: You Owe Me the Chance
card.instruction: Treat a past sacrifice, concession, or missed opportunity as a debt that should now be repaid with a real advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You had the good room on our last holiday. I'm choosing this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you liked the sofa bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was generous in both room allocation and commentary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The balcony room costs extra. I can pay the difference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. You cover the upgrade and I'll take the balcony. Last year's sofa bed can cover my share.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 claimed preference is reinterpreted at A3; B4 upgrade payment becomes A5 a debt-funded luxury.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges the sacrifice premise and B4 offers a concrete financial solution.

heightening.evidence: B4 willingness to pay is accepted while A5 assigns the benefit and treats past discomfort as their own contribution.

specificity.evidence: A1 repeated holidays and B4 balcony surcharge establish the lodging and money stakes.
